name: API Fetcher
description: Generic identifier-driven structured-API fetcher. Per-entity lookups against configured APIs (JSON + XML/RSS), multi-endpoint chaining, field mapping, raw-text flattening. Adding an API source = JSON config, not code.
usage_notes: Enriches entities from structured APIs keyed by an identifier (a channel id, feed URL, or registry number). Identifiers come from an entity seed column (Step 0) or a Step-1 pool-item field, so this Step-3 module is empty_ok (runs without prior URLs). Configure at least one provider (JSON config; see README for schemas and ready-made blocks). ALL provider knowledge — endpoints, params, field maps, auth, RSS tag names — is template configuration; no vertical is baked into code or defaults. providers: [] default is a loud no-op. emit_text_content (default false) mirrors raw_text into text_content + word_count so structured records survive Step-4 content-filter and reach Step-5 (needed for the LinkedIn-company bridge; text_content is in downloadable_fields so §7b hydration re-supplies it to content-analyzer). Bright Data bearer auth uses env var BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY (NOT BRIGHT_DATA_API_KEY).

options.name: providers
options.label: API Providers
options.description: Array of provider config objects: id, name, response_format (json|xml), identifier_source ({entity_field, item_field}), optional auth (none|query_param|header|bearer|basic), and endpoints[] (url, params, results_path, field_map, optional method [GET|POST], body, url_template / raw_text_template). Endpoints run in order; {identifier}, {max_items}, {endpoint_id.field} chain into the url, params, and POST body. No providers = loud no-op. See README for schema and examples.

options.name: provider_params
options.label: Provider parameters
options.description: Extra query params per provider id, merged into every endpoint request. E.g. {"companies-house": {"items_per_page": "20"}}.

options.name: max_items
options.label: Max items per list endpoint
options.description: Cap on records kept per endpoint (videos, episodes, filings). Also substituted into params via the {max_items} placeholder. Quota guard.

options.name: requests_per_minute
options.label: Rate limit (requests/min)
options.description: Global token-bucket rate limit across all providers, entities, and endpoints.

options.name: raw_text_max_chars
options.label: Raw text max characters
options.description: Truncate the flattened raw_text per item to this length (downstream Step 5 input size guard).

options.name: skip_providers_without_auth
options.label: Skip providers with missing credentials
options.description: When a provider declares auth with an env var that is not set, skip it with a warning (true) rather than calling the API unauthenticated (false).

options.name: emit_text_content
options.label: Emit text_content (for Step-4/5 consumption)
options.description: Also write text_content (mirror of the flattened raw_text) and word_count on each item. Step-4 content-filter keeps items by word_count and Step-5 content-analyzer/writer read text_content — so without this, structured API records are dropped at Step 4 and invisible to Step 5. Off = byte-identical legacy output (raw_text/data_json only). Turn ON for provider configs whose records should feed content generation (e.g. the Bright Data LinkedIn-company block).

options.name: domain_source
options.label: Provider lookup value source
options.description: Where the provider lookup value (the {identifier}) comes from. 'entity_field' (default) uses each provider's identifier_source (an entity seed column or a pool-item field) — byte-identical to the legacy contract. 'pool_url_host' derives the entity's registrable domain from the most frequent host across its own pool item urls (ignoring obvious third-party hosts like youtube/linkedin). It is FALLBACK-ONLY: a provider that resolves its own identifier keeps it; only a provider that resolves nothing falls back to the derived domain — so the mode composes with a multi-provider template. Use it for domain-keyed providers (e.g. a Bright Data LinkedIn-company lookup) when the seed website column does not survive to Step 3 — the entity is rebuilt from the pool with only {entity_name}, so an entity_field:'website' resolves to nothing. When no host is derivable the entity is skipped with a loud warning, never a silent empty fetch.
